# kb catalog — generated by `python tools/kb.py catalog`; do not edit

- **[bc]** [al-internal-blocks-extension-reuse](bc/al-internal-blocks-extension-reuse.md) — A public-looking method in a dependency can still be internal, and symbol browsers usually do not show it — you discover it as AL0161 at compile time, after designing around a call you cannot make  ·  `al  extension  dependency  symbols  symbolreference  troubleshooting  misleading`
- **[bc]** [al1024-dependency-version-trap](bc/al1024-dependency-version-trap.md) — AL1024 at publish shows the REQUESTED version, not the found one — the real cause is a dependency in app.json pinned newer than what the tenant runs; AL0247 that follows is just fallout  ·  `AL1024  AL0247  dependency  version  publish  dev-endpoint  error-message  misleading  app.json`
- **[bc]** [object-id-uniqueness](bc/object-id-uniqueness.md) — AL object IDs are unique per TYPE, not globally — but the idRanges reservation is per TENANT, so collisions with other installed extensions surface only at publish, never at compile  ·  `object-id  idRanges  tenant  collision  per-type  publish  AL  extension`
- **[bc]** [pte-permissionset-tabledata](bc/pte-permissionset-tabledata.md) — Every custom table needs an explicit tabledata entry in the extension's permission set or a PTE install fails on Production with PTE0004 — sandboxes never validate this, so it first appears on the environment you least want it on  ·  `pte  saas  permissionset  publish  extension  pte0004  error-message  misleading  troubleshooting`
- **[bc]** [pte-unpublish-previous-versions](bc/pte-unpublish-previous-versions.md) — Publish-PerTenantExtensionApps leaves every superseded version published-but-uninstalled forever unless you pass -unpublishPreviousVersions, so the environment slowly fills with inert duplicate tiles of the same app  ·  `pte  saas  publish  extension  version  unpublish  bccontainerhelper  troubleshooting`
- **[bc]** [public-symbol-nuget-feeds](bc/public-symbol-nuget-feeds.md) — Microsoft and AppSource (incl. LS Central) symbols are downloadable from two public NuGet feeds with no tenant login — but Find-BcNuGetPackage silently misses them without an explicit feed URL  ·  `symbols  nuget  feed  alpackages  BcContainerHelper  MSSymbols  AppSourceSymbols  download  no-docker`
- **[bc]** [report-excel-layout-data-table](bc/report-excel-layout-data-table.md) — A BC Excel report layout binds by the header-cell text, which must equal the dataset column names and stay in sync with the sheet's 'Data' table definition — opening one in Excel to reorder columns corrupts that binding  ·  `report  excel  layout  al  troubleshooting`
- **[bc]** [symbolreference-json-button-catalog](bc/symbolreference-json-button-catalog.md) — Every BC symbol .app contains SymbolReference.json with the full page/action tree — names, captions, RunObject targets — so a "what buttons does page X have" catalog is generatable offline, no tenant, no source code  ·  `symbols  SymbolReference  alpackages  pages  actions  buttons  catalog  RunObject  caption  tooltip  metadata`
- **[bc]** [symbolreference-json-trailing-padding](bc/symbolreference-json-trailing-padding.md) — Some publishers pad SymbolReference.json after the closing brace, so json.loads() dies with "Extra data" — a naive parser reports the package as having no symbols at all instead of reporting a parse error  ·  `symbols  symbolreference  alpackages  parsing  troubleshooting  misleading  silent-failure`
- **[lscentral]** [pos-run-objects-and-commands](lscentral/pos-run-objects-and-commands.md) — A POS button can open any BC object — including a Codeunit — via the RUNOBJ command and a POS Run Objects row; Run Codeunit on a POS Command is honoured only when Function Type is POS External, which is why built-ins like PRINT_Z show Run Codeunit = 0  ·  `pos  retail  runobject  actions  buttons  al  extension`
